status: experimental; not qualified for pilot execution
performed_by: Codex agent, synthetic local workloads only
result: 11 supervisor tests passed; combined supervisor, sandbox and egress run: 32 tests, 1 skipped
observations: Transient user systemd scope reported memory.max 33554432, memory.swap.max 0, pids.max 16 and cpu.max 100000 100000 from within the workload; a synthetic 128 MiB allocation was killed with signal 9 under the 32 MiB cap.
A synthetic fork loop hit EAGAIN with TasksMax=8; a setsid descendant did not write its delayed marker after timeout and scope termination.
Combined captured output was stopped at a configured 4096-byte cap. Output lock copied and hashed a synthetic file, rejected a symbolic link and rejected a multiply linked file.

An unprivileged private mount namespace successfully mounted a 1 MiB tmpfs; this is memory-backed and is not an established workspace-backed scratch quota. Workspace ext4 mount did not show quota options. The 100 GiB disk ceiling is not enforced by this supervisor.

The scope launcher restricts its affinity to selected CPUs and installs a libseccomp rule denying sched_setaffinity before executing the workload. A synthetic workload observed one assigned CPU, received EPERM on widening, and its exec descendant inherited that CPU. The user scope itself lacks a delegated cpuset controller; enforcement relies on inherited affinity and the seccomp rule.

A synthetic case ledger test charged time reservations and network bytes, closed and reopened the SQLite ledger, retained prior debits, denied over-budget operations, and reconciled an unused time reservation.
A synthetic successful parent detached a descendant and closed its output descriptors; the supervisor killed the remaining cgroup members before the descendant could write a delayed marker.
A synthetic workload closed both captured output descriptors then slept; the supervisor still timed it out in under two seconds with a 0.3-second limit.
A synthetic workload outlived a SIGKILL of its coordinator; the transient systemd scope RuntimeMaxSec watchdog killed it before its delayed write. Scope uses control-group kill and SIGKILL.

One hundred concurrent synthetic network debit attempts accepted exactly 50 bytes under a 50-byte shared limit; a three-second observed operation against a two-second reservation was charged three seconds. Case elapsed time uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME including suspend.
limitations: Transient scope properties can be rejected or ignored by the host; a successful invocation is not independent attestation of effective limits.
Output copies are chmod read-only and digest-recorded, not immutable to the same Unix owner. A separately controlled lock store and full output inventory remain necessary.
Timeout test covers one synthetic detached descendant and is not a proof of containment against hostile workloads. No third-party case ran and no human independent review occurred.

The ledger supplies durable accounting primitives but does not automatically wrap every executor action, independent reference capture or network transfer; until integrated across all phases aggregate limits are not enforced. Workspace scratch hard quota remains unverified.

After a coordinator crash, RuntimeMaxSec begins when the scope becomes active after the reservation: launch delay and scheduling can cause unmeasured deadline overshoot. A persisted reservation is conservatively retained; exact zero-overshoot enforcement is not established.

Forwarded application-byte accounting excludes lower-layer network framing, DNS, and traffic that bypasses the shared broker. All source and reference acquisition must be routed through the same reserved case ledger and broker.
